planting.note: Plant container shrubs in spring or fall in well-drained soil; prune hard in late winter since it blooms on new wood.

directions: Powerball is a new Proven Winners ColorChoice panicle hydrangea bred for unusually round, densely packed flower heads rather than the typical cone shape. Blooms open green-white and age through pink tones as the season progresses, held on sturdy stems that resist flopping. Because it flowers on new wood, cut it back hard in late winter to encourage the strongest round trusses the following summer. Give it full to part sun and consistent moisture for the best flower display.

common_name: Supertunia Vista Cool Jazz Petunia (Orchid-Pink Mounding Spreading Petunia)

planting.note: Set out nursery starts after last frost; no pinching or deadheading needed to keep it blooming.

directions: Cool Jazz brings the vigorous, weatherproof mounding habit of the Supertunia Vista line in a softer cool orchid-pink that blends easily with pastel companions instead of overpowering them. It self-cleans without deadheading and keeps flowering through summer heat and rain. Give it a large container or bed spot since trails can extend to 3 feet, and feed regularly for continuous bloom.

common_name: Reminiscent Yellow Garden Rose (Canary-Yellow Patio Shrub Rose)

planting.note: Plant container roses in full sun with good air circulation; blooms repeatedly on new wood through summer.

directions: Reminiscent Yellow is a Proven Winners ColorChoice garden rose (US Plant Patent PP37,279, bred by Christopher Warner) with clear canary-yellow blooms on an upright, patio-friendly shrub. It is bred for strong repeat bloom on new wood and tolerates close planting near patios and walkways. Keep it in full sun with moderate, even moisture, and remove spent canes each spring to keep the habit tidy and disease pressure low.

common_name: Urge to Splurge Spurge (Chartreuse-Bracted Cushion Euphorbia)

planting.note: Plant container perennials in well-drained soil in spring; wear gloves when handling cut stems since sap is irritating.

directions: Urge to Splurge is a new Proven Winners cushion spurge valued for a wide, spreading mound of chartreuse-yellow bracts in spring that signal the start of the season. As temperatures cool in fall, the foliage shifts into rich orange, red, and burgundy tones for extended seasonal interest. It thrives in lean, well-drained soil and full sun, and once established tolerates drought better than regular watering. Give it ample room since it spreads nearly twice as wide as it is tall.

common_name: Southern Blaze Bright Pink Phlox (Heat-Tolerant Annual Drummond's Phlox)

planting.note: Set out nursery starts after frost danger passes into sunny beds or containers.

directions: Southern Blaze Bright Pink is a new low-mounding Drummond's phlox bred specifically for heat and humidity tolerance in southern gardens. It stays compact and covers itself in glowing pink blooms through summer without the stretchiness or mildew problems that plague older annual phlox. Use it along border edges, in rock gardens, or in containers where its short, tidy habit shows well. Full sun and even moisture keep flowering dense all season.

common_name: Laguna Royale Lilac Lobelia (Dense Mounding Lilac-Flowered Edging Lobelia)

planting.note: Set out nursery starts in early spring; performs best before summer heat sets in.

directions: Laguna Royale Lilac is a new, denser and rounder-habited edging lobelia bred as part of the Laguna Royale series, staying smaller and tidier than older lobelia types. Soft lilac flowers cover the compact mound from spring into early summer, making it well suited to hanging baskets, window boxes, and border edges. It prefers cooler weather and part sun, and benefits from a light trim if it stretches during a hot spell.

common_name: Laguna Royale Azure Lobelia (Dense Mounding Azure-Blue Edging Lobelia)

planting.note: Set out nursery starts in early spring; performs best before summer heat sets in.

directions: Laguna Royale Azure pairs the same dense, rounded habit of the new Laguna Royale series with classic true-blue flowers, offering a more compact alternative to older trailing lobelia varieties. It blankets itself in azure blooms through cool spring weather, making an effective filler in mixed containers and edging beds. Part sun and consistently moist soil keep it flowering longest before summer heat slows it down.

common_name: Flavorette Pear'd Rose (Pink Edible-Petal Pear-Flavored Shrub Rose)

planting.note: Plant container roses in full sun in spring or fall; blooms continuously without deadheading.

directions: Flavorette Pear'd is a Spring Meadow Nursery rose bred for both ornamental display and culinary use, producing delicate pink, semi-double flowers with a genuine light pear flavor and soft texture. It blooms continuously through summer without the need for deadheading, and the petals can be used fresh in salads, desserts, or drinks. Plant it in full sun in mixed borders, cottage gardens, or dedicated cutting and herb gardens where the edible flowers are easy to reach.

common_name: Sgt. Pepper Dogwood (Cream-and-Pink Variegated Tatarian Dogwood)

planting.note: Plant container shrubs in moist, well-drained soil; best stem and leaf color develops in full sun.

directions: Sgt. Pepper is a Tatarian dogwood (US Plant Patent PP34,377), a sport of 'Elegantissima' found in Zundert, Netherlands, with bright green and cream variegated foliage edged in pale pink through spring and summer, then transitioning to a vivid burgundy and hot-pink combination in fall. Its bare burgundy-red stems add color through winter, and small white flowers appear in spring. It tolerates part shade but develops the strongest variegation and stem color in full sun with consistently moist soil, and makes an effective specimen, hedge, or focal planting.

common_name: Enchanted Meadow Rose (Color-Shifting Cream-Pink-Green Shrub Rose)

planting.note: Plant own-root container roses in full sun; needs regular watering until established.

directions: Enchanted Meadow is an own-root shrub rose (US Plant Patent PP37,009) from Will Radler, breeder of the original Knock Out rose, with cuplike blooms of 15 to 18 petals that open lined in deep pink and fade to a creamy, ice-green center as they age. The multicolor effect intensifies as each bloom matures, giving the shrub a shifting palette through the season. It forms a rounded, bushy habit with dark matte green foliage and strong disease resistance, flowering abundantly and continuously in full sun.

common_name: Martha Stewart Hybrid Tea Rose (Fragrant Ballet-Pink and Apricot Rose)

planting.note: Plant own-root container roses in full sun; deadhead spent blooms to encourage repeat flowering.

directions: Martha Stewart is a hybrid tea rose (US Plant Patent PP33,753, bred by Meilland, originally released in Europe as 'Jean de la Fontaine') with densely packed blooms of over 100 petals unfurling in shades of ballet pink and apricot. The flowers carry a strong fragrance with notes of citrus and honeysuckle, making it a strong choice for cutting gardens as well as borders. It keeps a compact, upright hybrid tea habit and repeats bloom through the growing season in full sun with regular care.

common_name: Parfuma Sunrise Rose (Fragrant Apricot-Pink Hybrid Tea Rose)

planting.note: Plant own-root container roses in full sun; new foliage emerges dark burgundy before greening.

directions: Parfuma Sunrise is a cold-hardy hybrid tea rose (US Plant Patent PP31,603) bred by Kordes and marketed under the Parfuma fragrance series, bearing large double apricot-pink blooms of 60 to 65 petals with an intense fragrance combining floral, citrus, and spicy tea notes. New foliage emerges in dark burgundy, offering striking contrast against the romantic flowers as the season progresses. It is noted for strong resistance to rust and mildew and reliable own-root performance, repeating bloom through the growing season in full sun.

common_name: Purple Aura Floribunda Rose (Spicy-Scented Magenta Shrub Rose)

planting.note: Plant container roses in full sun; shrub floribunda habit benefits from spring pruning.

directions: Purple Aura is a floribunda shrub rose (US Plant Patent PP37,080, bred by Alain Meilland) producing an abundance of rich magenta, 30-40 petal blooms with an unusual spicy fragrance reminiscent of clove and cinnamon. Its compact, bushy habit makes it suitable for mixed borders and mass plantings where its vivid color and scent can be appreciated up close. Grow it in full sun with moderate water, and prune in early spring to maintain a dense, floriferous shape.

common_name: Scarlet Drift Groundcover Rose (Compact Continuous-Blooming Red Rose)

planting.note: Plant container roses in full sun; low groundcover habit needs little pruning.

directions: Scarlet Drift is the newest member of the low-growing Drift groundcover rose series (US Plant Patent PP36,994), producing an abundant flush of single, deep red flowers that starts earlier in the season than other Drift varieties and reblooms reliably. Its compact, spreading habit stays under two feet tall, making it well suited to slopes, border edges, and mass groundcover plantings. Full sun and minimal maintenance keep it flowering from spring through frost.

common_name: Sugar Candy Rose (Color-Shifting Orange-to-Pink Patio Rose)

planting.note: Plant in containers or borders in full sun; stays under 2 feet tall.

directions: Sugar Candy is a patio-sized rose (US Plant Patent PP35,648, bred by Alain Meilland) with blooms notably larger than typical miniature roses that open bright orange-apricot and fade through salmon to candy pink as they age, covering the plant completely through the growing season. It stays under two feet tall, making it a strong choice for containers or mixed into annual beds for season-long color. The plant shows strong resistance to powdery mildew and black spot, keeping maintenance low in full sun with moderate watering.
